patterns.note: The hero section is a full-bleed, intricate typographic illustration on a dark background, setting a highly distinctive visual tone for the entire site.
The site heavily features large, decorative, and highly stylized display typefaces as primary content, with minimal use of standard body text.
A high-contrast black and white palette dominates the content, punctuated by a single bold red accent color for calls to action and footer sections.
Upon scrolling, the initially transparent header with a small logo and navigation shrinks slightly, gains a solid white background, and becomes sticky at the top of the viewport.
Product showcase sections feature a large, centered display of each font name, followed by a smaller, elegant descriptive line, creating a gallery-like presentation.

technique_notes: The hero section is built as a large, static graphic or a complex arrangement of text elements styled to appear as an illustration, occupying the full viewport height on load.
The main navigation bar transitions from a transparent, overlay state to a condensed, sticky header with a solid background and slightly reduced height as the user scrolls down the page.
Product showcase sections use large, centered text blocks for product names, with a secondary, smaller text line providing context, all presented against a clean white background.

design_tokens.type_scale: Extremely oversized, decorative display headings (~8-10x body) are the primary visual elements, complemented by small, legible sans-serifs for navigation and body text, and elegant, medium-sized serifs for descriptive text.
design_tokens.spacing: airy, with generous vertical padding between main content sections and ample negative space around large display type.

standout: The site's most distinctive feature is its hero section, which functions as an elaborate, full-page typographic illustration rather than a typical hero image or text block. This immediately establishes the brand's expertise and passion for typography, making the product (fonts) the art itself.
